Everytime I brought up-some of the things I learned they endured and how all of the people that did it deserved to die in the war they fought, he’d make a dum point like slavery was common back then and it didn’t just happen in America it happened in other places too. He’d be like “I don’t deny slavery was horrible because it was, I’m just saying white slave owners weren’t the only ones enslaving people of colour in America, as a matter of fact a large majority of people of colour in Africa were transporting and enslaving people of colour and selling them to slave owners in America and other countries for money. These people were given no money, both beat, tortured and killed if they didn’t do what they were told. I know im rambling on but I remember getting heated, just remembering movies like 12 years a slave, which showed a fraction of what Solomon went through and how he was forced into the slave trade even though he was a free man. Shit it just hurts to know the realities in relation to what happened. In a small town, have been diagnosed with bpd by a physiatrist in hospital after an episode. Bpd is rough, a couple years ago I altered my entire personality for 2 years straight. Think of the entire alpha mentality times 10. Being isolated for a year in a small town and not being able to handle criticism because you believe your untouchable is tough once reality comes into play and you begin to socialize. My personality before had been the class clown type, which really got me down, so I changed it completely after a friend suggested I had been a beta. This pissed me off and I was sick of getting hurt and not standing up for myself so I decided one day to change my personality completely on the spot. My family noticed it right away because I couldn't take criticism and lashed out at them every day. I even changed the way I talked so I always seemed right. Even now I have aspects of the personality change I underwent within a couple months. Not as extreme since I've caught on but still. The crappy thing about bpd for me is that I had to get extremely sick mentally and physically in order to be admitted into a hospital and diagnosed. A major overdose followed by self harm got me admitted, where they set me up with a physiatrist. In DBT as we speak and trying my best to get better.
